messages:
Sam L: Customer 'ClipStream' escalated — invoice for 2026-03 is ~1.2M tokens higher than their dashboard. They stream chunked responses over WebSocket and say the discrepancy correlates with mid-stream disconnects. Asked for logs but wanted us to triage ASAP.
Jason (billing): Can you paste the request_id(s) + ledger entries? We need to see if invoice lines match event stream.
Sam L: request_id: req_7b9c4a2f. Customer supplied a short transcript (redacted):
Sam L: ```
ws->server: {"type":"chunk","seq":41,"tokens":120,"final":false}
ws->server: {"type":"chunk","seq":42,"tokens":98,"final":false}
<connection drop>
(reconnect)
ws->server: {"type":"resume","session":"sess_9f8","last_seq":42}
ws->server: {"type":"chunk","seq":43,"tokens":50,"final":true}
```
Sam L: They claim ledger shows tokens from seq 41..43 twice (both pre-drop and post-resume), dashboard shows only one.
Jason (billing): Hmm. I pulled ledger rows for req_7b9c4a2f: LedgerEvent ids E129..E135 — I see chunk commits at 17:02:03 (seq41), 17:02:04 (seq42), then another set 17:02:05 (seq41) and 17:02:06 (seq42), then final seq43 at 17:02:07. So ledger has duplicated commits for seq41/42.
Priya (oncall): @Kenji can you look at the streaming resume path? This looks like a dedupe regression. If resume causes replay of buffered chunks plus final commit without recognizing previously committed chunk_ids we double-count.
Kenji (eng): On it. Quick note: the runtime checkpoint writes chunk commits to the write-ahead log on delivery, and resume logic currently replays in-memory buffer if it can't confirm an ack. The ack canonicalization lives in the shard index — if resume uses a different ephemeral session key we may not dedupe properly.
Kenji (eng): Repropped locally following their pattern — simple kill-before-final + resume -> ledger increments twice for same seq. Confirmed.
Priya (oncall): Can we capture a minimal repro script to share with infra? If it's reliable we should hotfix. Also recommend immediate customer remediation (credit) while we fix.
Sam L: Customer gave client lib version: clipstream-ws v1.2.3. They said it reuses same session id on resume. I have their consent to run a controlled repro against a staging key.
Kenji (eng): Quick repro (python):
Kenji (eng): ```python
import websocket, json, time
ws = websocket.create_connection('wss://api.redwood.ai/stream')
ws.send(json.dumps({"type":"chunk","seq":41,"tokens":120,"final":False}))
ws.send(json.dumps({"type":"chunk","seq":42,"tokens":98,"final":False}))
ws.close()  # simulate client crash
# reconnect and resume
ws = websocket.create_connection('wss://api.redwood.ai/stream')
ws.send(json.dumps({"type":"resume","session":"sess_test","last_seq":42}))
ws.send(json.dumps({"type":"chunk","seq":43,"tokens":50,"final":True}))
```
Kenji (eng): Run that a few times and check ledger rows.
AnomalyBot: Detected duplicate commit pattern for req_7b9c4a2f; pattern=chunk-replay-dup; severity=medium; suspect=stream-resume-logic; ticket=ANOM-8742.
Jason (billing): Customer wants immediate clarity. Can we estimate overbilled amount now? If double-counted seq41/42 that's (120+98)=218 tokens duplicated per session; customer reports ~5k affected sessions => ~1.09M tokens, matches their ~1.2M claim.
Priya (oncall): Kenji — can you scope whether all resume cases are affected or only those where the runtime failed to persist ack before crash? Also check whether this affects SSE and HTTP streaming or just WebSocket resume path.
Kenji (eng): Initial look: it's limited to the WebSocket resume path where the session id is replaced by ephemeral id on reconnect and the ledger commit id generation doesn't include the persistent session id. SSE paths use stable request ids so they're fine.
Kenji (eng): Plan: patch ledger commit to include (request_id, seq) as canonical unique key and make commit idempotent. Add a reconciliation job to scan last 7 days for duplicates and mark them for credit.
Sam L: Customer asked for a timeline and interim mitigation. They want a temporary block on double-commit for their org if possible.
Jason (billing): We can issue a provisional credit for the calculated delta and reverse if patch changes numbers. We need exact list of affected ledger event ids and amounts. @Kenji please export duplicate ledger rows for org clipstream (org_id org_44).
Kenji (eng): Exporting now. I'll add an annotation to each duplicate row and produce a csv. ETA 3 hours for export + reconciliation script.
Priya (oncall): Triage outcome: P1 for billing impact. Action items: Kenji = patch + export + reconciliation job; Jason = draft credit note and apply provisional credit; Sam = coordinate customer communication and confirm repro on staging; Kenji please also open PR with test reproducer.
Sam L: I'll tell customer we're investigating with a potential credit and will follow up with exact numbers in ~4 hours. :thumbsup:
Jason (billing): I'll prepare a provisional invoice adjustment and hold final until we have reconciled numbers.
Kenji (eng): Found root cause: resume handler was calling replay() which re-enqueues buffered chunks without checking ledger ack index. Pushing short fix to make replay check commit index before writing. Will try to land hotfix to prod in next 2 hours, then run reconciliation.
Priya (oncall): After hotfix, run smoke test with the python repro and also small load test. If green, we can close as workaround applied.
Sam L: Customer updated — appreciates quick response and said they can pause streaming retries on their side if we need more time.
Jason (billing): Once we have the csv, I'll compute token delta and apply credit. Keep me posted.
Kenji (eng): Hotfix deployed to staging; running smoke now. Will update thread with logs and CSV link when ready.
Sam L: Thank you team.
